reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about stress-driven segregation, precipitate formation, and embrittlement in single-phase HEAs, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover such specific alloy behaviour, so the lack of citations leaves all key premises unsupported.
premises: Sustained high-amplitude loading drives elemental segregation to grain boundaries in a nominal single-phase HEA
This segregation leads to nanoscale, brittle intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries
The precipitates reduce grain boundary cohesion, causing a ductile-to-brittle fracture transition
The mechanism operates above a threshold of stress and temperature that drives significant atomic diffusion
